milestones.notes: async/await syntax landed in 3.5 (PEP 492); asyncio itself was added provisional one release earlier, in 3.4, written with @asyncio.coroutine + yield from.
threading module wraps real OS threads, but the GIL serializes all Python bytecode execution across them.

multiprocessing (PEP 371, 2.6) was the first stdlib way to use multiple cores, via separate processes rather than threads. concurrent.futures (3.2) made pooling either one easier. PEP 703 free-threading (3.13 experimental, 3.14 officially supported but optional) is the first mode giving real parallel threads for Python code itself.
ssl.PROTOCOL_TLSv1_1/TLSv1_2 constants added in 3.4 and backported to 2.7.9 (2015-01, PEP 466), which also added SNI and modern certificate verification to the 2.7 ssl module.
preliminary/experimental in 3.7.0, dependent on being linked against OpenSSL 1.1.1 (not yet finalized at release); solid by 3.10.
socket module AF_INET6/getaddrinfo support, platform-dependent (exposed via socket.has_ipv6). Dedicated ipaddress module added in 3.3; IPv6 scoped-address (%<scope_id>) support added in 3.9.

str became unicode text by default in 3.0 (PEP 3137), with a separate immutable bytes type. Python 2.0-2.7 had a separate `unicode` type alongside 8-bit `str`. PEP 393 (3.3) made the internal representation memory-efficient (flexible string representation).

pip bundled by default via the new ensurepip module (PEP 453). The venv module itself landed one release earlier, in 3.3 (PEP 405); 2.x and 3.0-3.3 have neither, relying on separately-installed easy_install/pip and third-party virtualenv.

PEP 585 let builtin collections act as generic types (list[int]) without importing typing. The typing module itself (with its own Generic/List[int]) dates to 3.5 (PEP 484); PEP 695's `class Foo[T]:` syntax followed in 3.12.
first Python release with an official amd64 Windows installer, alongside the existing x86 one.
full Apple Silicon support, including the universal2 fat-binary installer, arrived in the 3.9.1 patch release specifically, not 3.9.0.
3.9 and 3.10 shipped only an arm64 embeddable zip; a full arm64 installer followed in 3.11.

python.org itself never ships Linux binaries at all, at any version (source tarball only). Prebuilt arm64 Linux archives exist only via the third-party python-build-standalone project, which starts covering CPython at 3.8.

os_support.windows: Windows 95/98/NT/2000, x86 installer only; no 64-bit Windows build
os_support.macos: none from python.org; classic Mac OS support existed only via the third-party MacPython project
os_support.linux: any Unix with a C compiler (source tarball only); no official binaries

added: cyclic garbage collector for container objects
a unicode string type, separate from the existing 8-bit str
limitations: no generators (added 2.2, default 2.3)
no builtin bool type (2.3)
no unified type/class model -- classes and types are different things until new-style classes (2.2)
GIL-bound threading only; no multiprocessing (2.6) for real multi-core use
no bundled packaging tool of any kind (distutils exists but no pip/easy_install yet)

os_support.windows: Windows 95/98/NT/2000, x86 installer only
os_support.macos: none from python.org

added: richer __future__ statement mechanism used to phase in later syntax changes
limitations: nested scopes not default yet (default in 2.2)
same threading/GIL and packaging limitations as 2.0
still no generators or new-style classes

os_support.windows: Windows 95/98/NT/2000, x86 installer only
os_support.macos: none from python.org

added: new-style classes unifying types and classes (PEP 252/253)
limitations: generators require a future-import until 2.3
no builtin set or bool types yet
no decorators (2.4), no with-statement (2.5)
still GIL-only threading

os_support.windows: Windows 95/98/NT/2000, x86 installer only
os_support.macos: none from python.org

added: generators enabled by default, no future-import needed
sets module (set/frozenset as library types, not yet builtins)
limitations: set/frozenset are not builtins until 2.4 (`sets` module only)
no decorators until 2.4
no sqlite3 in the standard library until 2.5
no with-statement/context managers until 2.5

os_support.windows: 98/NT/2000/XP; x86 and, new in this release, Itanium (ia64) installers
os_support.macos: PowerPC/Intel universal installer ("macpython" build)

limitations: no with-statement or conditional (ternary) expression until 2.5
no absolute/relative import control until 2.5 (PEP 328)
packaging still distutils + separately-installed easy_install; no pip

os_support.windows: 98/NT/2000/XP; x86, amd64 (first 64-bit Windows installer) and ia64
os_support.macos: universal (PowerPC/Intel) installer

added: with-statement and context managers (PEP 343), behind `from __future__ import with_statement`
conditional expressions `x if c else y` (PEP 308)
limitations: with-statement needs a future-import in 2.5 itself (default from 2.6)
no importlib; the import system is still C-level only
packaging still distutils/easy_install, no pip

os_support.windows: 2000/XP/Vista; x86 and amd64 installers
os_support.macos: universal installer, now stating a Mac OS X 10.3 minimum

added: multiprocessing module (PEP 371) -- the first stdlib way to use more than one core
`except X as e` syntax (PEP 3110) backported for 2/3-compatible code
`__future__` imports (print_function, unicode_literals, ...) to ease porting to 3.x
limitations: GIL still serializes threads; multiprocessing is the only way to use multiple cores
no TLS SNI support in ssl (arrives 2.7.9)
no async I/O framework (asyncio is 3.4)

os_support.windows: 2000/XP/Vista/7 across its lifetime; x86 and amd64 installers
os_support.macos: installers spanning Mac OS X 10.3, 10.5, 10.6 and (from 2.7.9-era builds) 10.9 minimums over its lifetime; no build ever supported Apple Silicon

added: unified except/finally in one try statement
limitations: ssl had no SNI (Server Name Indication) or modern certificate-verification defaults until 2.7.9 (2014-12, PEP 466) -- a real problem for HTTPS clients on name-based virtual hosting before then
no async/await; only generator-based coroutine patterns (send/throw from 2.5)
str is 8-bit bytes and unicode is a separate type -- the classic Python 2 encode/decode footguns
official end-of-life 2020-01-01; code still targeting 2.7 today runs on an unsupported, unpatched interpreter
no venv/pip bundled (bundled pip is a 3.4-only feature); packaging relies on separately-installed setuptools/pip

os_support.windows: 2000/XP/Vista; x86 and amd64 installers
os_support.macos: none published for 3.0 (macOS installers resume at 3.1)

added: print as a function, not a statement
str is unicode text by default; separate immutable bytes type (PEP 3137)
true division is the default for `/` (PEP 238)
old-style classes removed -- one unified object model
limitations: virtually no third-party libraries were ported yet at release -- real-world adoption of 3.0 itself was very limited
no `u''` string literal prefix (removed; restored in 3.3 for 2/3-compatible code)
several operations were measurably slower than 2.6, not addressed until 3.1/3.2
no async/await (3.5), no venv (3.3), no pip bundling (3.4), no yield from (3.3)

os_support.windows: 2000/XP/Vista; x86 and amd64 installers
os_support.macos: universal installer, Mac OS X 10.3 minimum

added: io module reimplemented in C for speed
multiple context managers in one with-statement
limitations: third-party package availability under Python 3 is still very thin
no importlib-based import system yet
no stdlib venv (virtualenv is still third-party only)

os_support.windows: XP/Vista/7; x86 and amd64 installers
os_support.macos: universal installers, Mac OS X 10.3 and (separately) 10.6 minimum variants

added: a new GIL implementation (fixed time-slice switching, replacing the old opcode-count heuristic, fixing pathological CPU-bound-thread contention)
ssl.SSLContext and client-side SNI support added to the ssl module
limitations: no yield from (3.3)
no stdlib venv -- virtualenv is still third-party (3.3)
no asyncio; only low-level select/selectors-based I/O
the GIL rewrite improved fairness between threads but did not add multi-core parallelism for Python code

os_support.windows: XP/Vista/7; x86 and amd64 installers
os_support.macos: universal installers, Mac OS X 10.5 and 10.6 minimum variants

added: PEP 393 flexible string representation -- large memory-efficiency win for unicode strings
limitations: no asyncio yet (provisional in 3.4)
no pip bundled by default (ensurepip is 3.4)
no async/await syntax (3.5)

os_support.windows: XP/Vista/7/8; x86 and amd64 installers
os_support.macos: universal installers, Mac OS X 10.5 and 10.6 minimum variants

added: pip bundled by default via the new ensurepip module (PEP 453)
limitations: asyncio's API is explicitly provisional and changed across 3.4.x point releases -- not a stable target yet
no async/await syntax -- asyncio coroutines are written with `@asyncio.coroutine` and `yield from`
pathlib is also provisional at this point

os_support.windows: Vista and later -- built with MSVC 14.0/Visual Studio 2015, which dropped Windows XP from the stock installer. Operator-tested exception: a custom 3.5 XP backport (patched so asyncio works) runs on Windows XP for this project -- see TESTED-WINDOWS.md
os_support.macos: Mac OS X 10.6 and later

added: async/await syntax (PEP 492) -- asyncio module itself still provisional
limitations: asyncio and typing are both still provisional APIs and can change without a deprecation cycle
no f-strings (3.6)
dict ordering is not guaranteed by the language yet (official in 3.7)
dropped Windows XP support in the stock installer -- XP is only reachable via unofficial/backport builds

os_support.windows: Vista and later; x86/amd64 installer plus embeddable zip
os_support.macos: Mac OS X 10.9 (amd64 installer) alongside a 10.6-minimum universal installer

added: dict became insertion-ordered as a CPython implementation detail (made an official language guarantee in 3.7)
limitations: dict ordering is only a CPython implementation detail here, not a language guarantee -- other implementations weren't required to match it
typing module is still evolving rapidly
no dataclasses (3.7), no breakpoint() (3.7)

os_support.windows: Vista and later; x86/amd64 installer plus embeddable zip. Operator-tested: stock 3.7.0 x86 confirmed with working asyncio on Windows Vista for this project -- see TESTED-WINDOWS.md
os_support.macos: Mac OS X 10.9 (amd64 installer) alongside a 10.6-minimum universal installer

added: dict insertion order made an official language guarantee
async and await become reserved keywords (can no longer be used as identifiers)
limitations: TLS 1.3 support in ssl is preliminary/experimental and depends on OpenSSL 1.1.1, which wasn't finalized when 3.7.0 shipped
making async/await reserved keywords breaks any code still using them as variable names
no walrus operator or positional-only parameters (3.8)

os_support.windows: Vista/7/8/8.1 and later; x86/amd64 installer plus embeddable zip. Operator-tested: stock 3.8.0 x86 confirmed with working asyncio on Windows 7 and 8/8.1 for this project -- see TESTED-WINDOWS.md. Last CPython line with unmodified upstream support for 7/8/8.1: 3.9 requires Windows 8+ APIs and won't run there without a third-party fork
os_support.macos: Mac OS X 10.9 installer, plus python-build-standalone amd64/arm64 archives
os_support.linux: source tarball only from python.org; python-build-standalone (third-party) adds prebuilt amd64/arm64 archives starting this major

added: TLS 1.3 post-handshake authentication support in ssl
ProactorEventLoop becomes the default Windows asyncio event loop, adding UDP support
limitations: still no free-threading or true parallel threads for Python code -- the GIL is unchanged
no structural pattern matching (3.10), no exception groups (3.11)
last major with reliable stock support on Windows 7/8/8.1

os_support.windows: Windows 8 and later only -- the stock installer statically links api-ms-win-core-path-l1-1-0.dll, which doesn't exist on Vista/7, so 3.9 won't run there without a third-party fork (bpo-32592 dropped Vista/7)
os_support.macos: 10.9+ generally; full Apple Silicon (arm64) support and the universal2 fat-binary installer arrived specifically in the 3.9.1 patch release, not 3.9.0
os_support.linux: source tarball only from python.org; python-build-standalone adds amd64/arm64/armv7/ppc64le/riscv64/s390x archives

added: builtin generic collections, e.g. list[int] without importing typing (PEP 585)
Windows ARM64 build capability (embeddable zip only, no installer yet)
limitations: 3.9.0 itself has no Apple Silicon/arm64 macOS build -- 3.9.1 or later is required for that
Windows ARM64 at this point is an embeddable zip, not a full installer (that's 3.11)
no structural pattern matching (3.10)
dropped Windows Vista and 7 outright

os_support.windows: Windows 8 and later; x86/amd64/arm64 (embed-only) installers and embeddable zips
os_support.macos: macOS 11 (Big Sur) baseline for the universal2 installer; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64 archives
os_support.linux: source tarball only from python.org; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64/armv7/ppc64le/riscv64/s390x

added: union types written as X | Y (PEP 604)
limitations: match/case is new syntax -- code using it cannot run on 3.9 or earlier at all, not just a library-availability problem
still no exception groups (3.11)
still GIL-bound; free-threading isn't even experimental yet

os_support.windows: Windows 8 and later; adds a full Windows ARM64 installer (previously embeddable-zip only) alongside amd64/x86
os_support.macos: macOS 11 (Big Sur) baseline for the universal2 installer; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64
os_support.linux: source tarball only from python.org; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64/armv7/ppc64le/riscv64/s390x

added: tomllib in the standard library (read-only TOML parser)
fine-grained error locations in tracebacks (PEP 657), pointing at the exact sub-expression
about 25% faster on average (10-60% range) via the Specializing Adaptive Interpreter (PEP 659)
limitations: tomllib is read-only -- no TOML writer in the standard library
no free-threading or JIT yet (3.13)
no template strings (3.14)

os_support.windows: Windows 8 and later; x86/amd64/arm64 installers and embeddable zips
os_support.macos: macOS 11 (Big Sur) baseline for the universal2 installer; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64
os_support.linux: source tarball only from python.org; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64/armv7/ppc64le/riscv64/s390x

added: PEP 701: more flexible f-strings (nested same quotes, multi-line expressions, backslashes inside {})
PEP 695 type-parameter syntax for generics, e.g. `class Foo[T]:`
the buffer protocol exposed to pure-Python code (PEP 688)
distutils removed from the standard library
further interpreter and error-message quality improvements
limitations: distutils removal breaks old packaging code that still imports it directly -- must migrate to setuptools
PEP 695 generics syntax is new and unusable on 3.11 and earlier
still no free-threaded build (that's 3.13, experimental)

os_support.windows: Windows 10/11 is the primary supported target for new features (installs on 8+ per the 3.9-era floor). Operator-tested: stock 3.13.0 x86 confirmed with working asyncio on Windows 10 and 11 for this project -- see TESTED-WINDOWS.md
os_support.macos: macOS 11 (Big Sur) baseline for the universal2 installer; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64
os_support.linux: source tarball only from python.org; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64/armv7/ppc64le/riscv64/s390x

added: experimental free-threaded build (PEP 703, --disable-gil, separate python3.13t binary; not the default)
experimental JIT compiler (PEP 744, --enable-experimental-jit, copy-and-patch, off by default)
much-improved interactive REPL (multiline editing, colored tracebacks, F1/F2/F3 features)
Tier 3 support for iOS (PEP 730) and Android (PEP 738)
19 long-deprecated "dead battery" modules removed (PEP 594: cgi, telnetlib, imghdr, ...), plus 2to3 removed
limitations: free-threading is experimental, has a substantial single-threaded performance hit, and breaks any C extension not rebuilt for it
the JIT is experimental, off by default, and its own docs describe the performance gains so far as modest
several stdlib modules developers relied on for decades (cgi, telnetlib, ...) are simply gone, not deprecated-but-present

os_support.windows: Windows 10/11 primary target, same floor as 3.13
os_support.macos: macOS 11 (Big Sur) baseline for the universal2 installer; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64
os_support.linux: source tarball only from python.org; python-build-standalone covers amd64/arm64/armv7/ppc64le/riscv64/s390x

added: free-threading (PEP 703) promoted from experimental to officially supported, phase two per PEP 779 -- still an optional, non-default build
deferred evaluation of annotations by default (PEP 649/749)
concurrent.interpreters -- subinterpreters exposed in the standard library (PEP 734)
limitations: free-threading is officially supported but still optional/non-default -- most C extensions still need an explicit free-threaded rebuild
t-strings are new syntax: a Template object isn't a str, so tools and libraries built around f-strings don't understand it for free
the JIT introduced in 3.13 is still experimental in 3.14, not promoted alongside free-threading
